condition: repeated home blood pressure readings around 154 over 96 without symptoms
level_rationale: Repeated morning upper-arm blood pressure readings staying around 154 over 96 mmHg at home every day for 2 weeks in a 52-year-old adult represent sustained stage-2 home blood pressure elevation requiring non-emergent outpatient general-physician evaluation and antihypertensive management rather than home self-care alone or emergency department care, whereas repeated morning home readings staying around 118 over 74 mmHg for 2 weeks reflect normal adult blood pressure needing only routine healthy self-care.

design_note: Three atomic positive reference facts cover age 52, daily morning home upper-arm blood pressure monitoring for 2 weeks, and sustained readings around 154 over 96 without naming hypertension or stating 'without symptoms', with a 1-word span difference (17 vs 18 words) and natural unstacked patient phrasing. Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice and Rule D, changing only the single measured blood pressure reading in f3 from '154 over 96' to normal '118 over 74' shifts care unambiguously from outpatient physician evaluation (level 2) to routine self-care (level 1) without bundling extra symptoms.
